title: The Super Car's Trap
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Inspector Yokomizo) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed, attributed edge between the entities involved (person/location/object), sharing an `order` integer so edges belonging to the same real-world occurrence can be grouped without a reifying node. The old wiki-summary case file (cases/ep197-198_the_super_cars_trap.json) named the correct culprit (Hisashi Suguro, s1) but was extremely thin: it omitted that Suguro himself was a fourth scam victim (Teraizumi swindled him out of the Ferrari Dino that became the murder weapon/scene) -- the real motive is identical in kind to the three red-herring suspects', not just 'a documented grievance'. It also collapsed the actual trick (car-cover-as-gas-chamber over the Dino, muffled engine sound mistaken by the guard for an unknown car, staged as a driving accident) into a vague single 'traps him in the car' event, missed the coal-tar-stain / headlight-crack-and-thread / engine-sound-test physical clues entirely, omitted witness Kazuo Noda, and had only one generic clue node with no comparative content. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: The coal-tar stain leaking from the Dino's exhaust pipe is cut off in a perfectly straight line, and an identical straight-edged tar smear is found on the underside of Suguro's car cover near the muffler area -- the two stains match, proving that specific cover was sealed over the Dino at the time the exhaust was running.

Noda testifies the unfamiliar grayish car he saw around 10am had an engine sound he'd never heard before, unlike the Dino's; a live test starting the Dino's engine and then draping the same plastic cover over it reproduces exactly the muffled sound Noda heard, proving the 'unknown car' was the cover-shrouded Dino all along.

A thread snagged in the fresh crack on the Dino's headlight cover matches a tear in the trousers Suguro claimed to have changed out of the night before, placing him physically striking the car while sealing the cover.
